newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mixed.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mixed.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mixed in heavy trading on Thursday with active domestic A shares markets and new A share issues supporting the repo rates, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract rose to 11.49 percent from 11.00 percent on Wednesday.
Combined turnover rose to 12.73 million lots from 7.91 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said the market rates were at high levels after surges last week and early this week and were likely to continue to move at current levels in the short term.
"A rising A share market and continued A share issues will be major factors supporting rates at high levels in the next few days," one trader said.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mixed due to institutional support and market sentiment was weak with liquidity flowing out into the A share markets, traders said.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 rose slightly to 123.18 yuan from 123.16 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market rose to 2.28 million lots from 1.72 million.
